mainTopic: Why a fine goes to the victim, and a new משנה about oxen owned by a חרש, שוטה, or קטן: when a guardian is appointed, and whose property pays when their ox is a מועד.
overview: The amud opens with the end of an earlier discussion: the fine goes to the victim so that the sinner gains nothing. רב מרי explains why the money is not simply given to the poor: money owed to 'the poor' in general has no one who can demand it. Then a new משנה teaches that a פקח whose ox gores the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן must pay, but in the reverse case the owner is פטור. If their ox keeps goring, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס, and רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about whether the ox stays a מועד once the owner becomes competent. The משנה also rules that a stadium ox that kills is not put to death. The גמרא asks how the משנה can both exempt these owners and appoint a guardian. רבא answers that the guardian is appointed only for oxen already known to gore, to make them מועד. רבי יוחנן and רבי יוסי בר חנינא then argue over whose best property pays, the orphans' or the guardian's. A proposal to swap their opinions is rejected by רבא, who explains that a מזיק is different from a normal debt, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The sinner should not profit
steps.stepSummary: The earlier discussion ends with its reason: the fine is paid so that the sinner does not come out ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the sinner should not be rewarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reason it gave just before this line. The fine stays in place so that the person who did wrong does not end up gaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought the payment should be cancelled for this victim. But cancelling it would mean the חוטא keeps his money and gains from his sin. So the payment is kept.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner, the one who did the wrong
Rewarded, comes out ahead

phrases.english: So that the sinner should not be rewarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the reasoning that began in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fine is still paid so that the sinner does not profit from his sin.

steps.title: Why not give the money to the poor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason: if the only goal is that the sinner not profit, he could just give the money to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him give it to the poor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given. If all we want is that the sinner lose the money, he could give it to the poor instead of to the victim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'so the sinner does not profit' only requires that he lose the money. It does not say who must receive it. So the challenge asks why the victim specifically has to get it.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him give it
Poor people

phrases.english: Then let him give it to the poor!
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the sinner, and 'it' is the fine money he owes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 1 by suggesting another place for the money to go.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that the fine is paid so the sinner does not profit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason is fully met if the money goes to the poor, so why must the victim get it?

steps.title: רב מרי: money with no one to claim it
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי answers that money owed to the poor in general has no specific claimant, so in practice it would never be collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: Because it would be money that has no claimants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the challenge. Giving the money to 'the poor' does not work, because no particular person could demand it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money belonged to the poor in general, any poor person who asked for it could be turned away with 'I'll give it to someone else.' Then the sinner would never really pay, and he would profit after all. Giving it to the victim means there is a real person who can collect it.

keyTerms.meaning: Money
Claimants, people who can demand payment

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי מָמוֹן שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹבְעִים.
phrases.english: Because it is money that has no claimants.
phrases.notes: No single poor person owns this money, so nobody could take him to court over it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical enforcement: the alternative fails in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving to the poor would fully satisfy the goal that the sinner not profit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money owed to the poor in general has no claimant and would never be collected, so the sinner would profit. It must go to the victim.
steps.whatToRemember: The goal that the sinner not profit only works if a real person can demand the money. Money that 'belongs to the poor' in general has no one who can claim it.

steps.title: משנה: oxen of competent and non-competent owners
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a פקח's ox that gores the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן makes its owner liable. In the reverse case the owner is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the ox of a competent person gored the ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, the owner is liable. If the ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor gored the ox of a competent person, the owner is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares damage done by a competent person's ox with damage done by the ox of someone the הלכה does not treat as fully responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not symmetrical. When the victim is a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, the competent owner still pays. When the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן does the damage, its owner is פטור, because these owners are not held responsible for guarding their animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A competent person, fully responsible in הלכה
A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor: people not treated as fully responsible
Gored
Liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The exemption depends on who owns the ox that did the damage, not on who was hurt. A competent owner pays even when the victim is a חרש, שוטה, or קטן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An ox of a competent person that gored

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: an ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor: he is liable.
But one of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor
that gored an ox of a competent person: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹר שֶׁל פִּקֵּחַ שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A competent owner pays for damage to the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן. The ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן that damages makes its owner פטור.

steps.title: Appointing a guardian when their ox gores
steps.stepSummary: When the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן gores, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס, and witnesses testify about the ox in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor gored, the court appoints a guardian for them, and witnesses testify to them in front of the guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with what happens when an ox belonging to a non-competent owner keeps goring. בית דין sets up a guardian to stand in for the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner is exempt, but the ox can still be made a מועד through formal warning. So בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס, and the testimony about the goring is given in front of him, since he takes the owner's place. This sets up the next issue: what the status of the ox becomes once it has a guardian.

keyTerms.meaning: The court
They appoint, set up
A guardian or steward who manages someone's property
They testify, or give formal warning before witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even when an owner is not held responsible, בית דין still appoints someone who can stand in the owner's place, so warnings about the ox can be given before him.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּגַח –
phrases.english: An ox of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor that gored:
the court appoints a guardian for them,
and they testify to them in the presence of the guardian.
phrases.notes: This is the testimony that the ox gored. Here it is given to the guardian, since the owner himself can't receive it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, explaining how בית דין handles the goring ox of a non-competent owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a goring ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס, and testimony about the ox is given in his presence.
steps.whatToRemember: A non-competent owner is פטור, but בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס to stand in for him, and testimony about the ox is given before that guardian.

steps.title: When the owner becomes competent, the ox goes back to being a תם
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that once the חרש, שוטה, or קטן becomes competent, the ox that was made a מועד goes back to being a תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the deaf-mute regained his hearing, the שוטה became sane, or the קטן grew up, the ox goes back to being a תם. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the case from step 5. An ox was made a מועד in front of the אפוטרופוס, and now the owner himself has become competent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, the מועד status was tied to the time the ox was under the אפוטרופוס. Once the real owner can take care of it himself, the ox starts fresh as a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: Became a פִּקֵּחַ, meaning he became a fully competent person (here: the deaf-mute regained his hearing)
Became sane and settled in his mind
The status of being a תָּם, an ox not known to gore

phrases.english: If the deaf-mute regained his hearing,
the mentally incompetent person became sane,
or the minor grew up,
the ox has gone back to being a tam,
phrases.notes: This is the ox that was made a מועד in front of the אפוטרופוס in the last step.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְפַּקֵּחַ הַחֵרֵשׁ, נִשְׁתַּפָּה הַשּׁוֹטֶה וְהִגְדִּיל הַקָּטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case of the ox made מועד in front of an אפוטרופוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, once the owner becomes competent, the ox goes back to being a תם.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the ox keeps its forewarned status
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and says the ox stays a מועד even after the owner becomes competent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: it stays in its earlier status, so it is still a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the argument. רבי יוסי says nothing changes when the owner becomes competent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the ox's goring record belongs to the ox itself. A change in the owner's condition does not erase what the ox has shown it does.

keyTerms.meaning: In its established status (here: still a מוּעָד)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It remains in its established status.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי הוּא בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the ox stays a מועד even after the owner becomes competent.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת here. רבי מאיר says the ox goes back to being a תם, and רבי יוסי says it stays a מועד.

steps.title: A stadium ox that kills is not put to death
steps.stepSummary: An ox trained to fight in a stadium is not killed if it gores a person to death, because the פסוק speaks of an ox that gores on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stadium ox is not put to death, because the פסוק says 'if an ox gores,' meaning it gored on its own, and not that people made it gore.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches a new law. A fighting ox that people trained and pushed to gore is not given the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כי יגח describe an ox that chooses to gore by itself. A stadium ox gores because people stirred it up, so it is not included in that פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A stadium ox, trained to fight in an arena
'If it gores': the פסוק about an ox that kills a person
That others made it gore

phrases.english: A stadium ox
is not liable to be put to death,
as it is said: "If it gores"
and not that others made it gore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the משנה, separate from the case of the חרש, שוטה, or קטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stadium ox that kills is not put to death, because it was made to gore by others.

steps.title: The two halves of the משנה seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The first clause implies that no אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם. The later clause implies that one is appointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is difficult. You said that if the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן gored the ox of a competent person, the owner is פטור. That shows we do not appoint an אפוטרופוס for a תם so that payment can be collected from the ox's body. But look at the later clause: if their ox gored, בית דין appoints an אפוטרופוס and witnesses testify in front of him. That shows we do appoint an אפוטרופוס for a תם to collect from its body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts its discussion. It points out that the משנה's first ruling (step 4) and its later ruling (step 5) seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם pays only from the body of the goring ox. If the first clause says פטור, then no one is set up to collect from the ox. The later clause does set up an אפוטרופוס, and that seems to be for exactly this kind of collection.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult: the source contradicts itself
Evidently; this shows that
A guardian appointed by בית דין
To collect from the body of the goring ox itself
Now say the later clause

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is only about a תם, which pays from its own body. No one is asking about a מועד here yet.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן,
phrases.english: You said: the ox of a deaf-mute, an incompetent, or a minor
that gored the ox of a competent person is exempt;
evidently we do not appoint a guardian for a tam
to collect from its body.
phrases.notes: A תם pays half damages only out of the goring ox itself, so collecting from its body is the only way it pays.

phrases.english: Now say the later clause:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּגַח –
phrases.english: the ox of a deaf-mute, an incompetent, or a minor that gored:
the court appoints a guardian for them,
and witnesses testify about them in front of the guardian.
Evidently we do appoint a guardian for them for a tam,
to collect from its body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rulings of steps 4 and 5 and sets them against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the משנה's two rulings about the ox of a חרש, שוטה, or קטן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause's פטור implies no אפוטרופוס is appointed for a תם. The later clause's appointment of an אפוטרופוס implies one is appointed.

steps.title: רבא: the guardian is appointed only for oxen known to gore
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the later clause is about oxen that already have a goring reputation. The אפוטרופוס is appointed to make them מועד, so that future goring is paid from the best property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, this is what the משנה means: if they became known as goring oxen, we appoint an אפוטרופוס for them, witnesses testify in front of him, and we make the ox a מועד. That way, when it gores again, the owner pays from his best property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction. He reads the later clause as speaking about a different situation from the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause stays true: no אפוטרופוס is appointed just to collect from a תם's body. The later clause is about oxen that have already gored many times. There the אפוטרופוס is appointed to turn the ox into a מועד, so that future damage is paid in full from the owner's best property.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the משנה is teaching: a rereading of the text
They became known as goring oxen
We make them a מוּעָד
From the best-quality property

steps.whatToRemember: No אפוטרופוס is appointed to collect from a תם. One is appointed for oxen already known to gore, to make them מועד for the future.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the purpose of the אפוטרופוס in step 5. He is there to set up the ox's מועד status, not to collect for a תם.

phrases.english: Rava said, this is what it is teaching:
and if they became known as goring oxen,
we appoint a guardian for them,
and witnesses testify about them in front of the guardian,
and we make them forewarned;
so that when it goes back and gores again,
the owner pays from the best property.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the later clause so it refers to a different case (oxen already known as goring oxen).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause seemed to appoint an אפוטרופוס to collect from a תם's body.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אפוטרופוס is appointed only for oxen known to gore, in order to make them מועד so future damages are paid from the owner's best property.

steps.title: Whose best property pays?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose best-quality property pays when the orphans' מועד ox does damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: From whose best property is the payment taken?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question about רבא's answer. This sets up the disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the אפוטרופוס is appointed so that later damage is paid from the best property. The question is whose best property that means: the orphans' property, or the guardian's own property. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: the best-quality property (the same idea as עִידִּית)
who / whose

phrases.english: From whose best-quality property?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבא's point in step 10, that a מועד ox pays from the best property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail left open in רבא's תירוץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the payment comes from the orphans' best property or the אפוטרופוס's best property.

steps.title: Two views: the orphans' property or the guardian's
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the payment comes from the orphans' best property. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says it comes from the guardian's best property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: from the orphans' best property. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says: from the guardian's best property.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's version, the court takes the payment directly from what the orphans own. In רבי יוסי בר חנינא's version, the אפוטרופוס pays from his own best property, so the orphans' property is not touched now.

keyTerms.meaning: orphans (here, young orphans who own the oxen)
a guardian appointed by the court

steps.confusionAlert: "The guardian's best property" means the guardian's own land, not the orphans' land that he manages.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: from the best property of the orphans,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מֵעֲלִיַּית אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina says: from the best property of the guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: from the orphans' best property. רבי יוסי בר חנינא: from the guardian's best property.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן elsewhere says the court does not collect from orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. Elsewhere he says the court collects from orphans' property only for a loan with interest or for a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי that the court does not deal with orphans' property unless interest is eating it up. And רבי יוחנן said: only for a loan document with interest, or for a woman's כתובה because of her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view from step 12, using another ruling of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי says the court does not collect from orphans' property unless interest is eating it up. רבי יוחנן says the court collects from orphans only in two cases: a loan document with interest, or a widow's כתובה, since until she is paid she gets food from the estate. Damage from an ox is neither of these cases, so how could רבי יוחנן say to collect from the orphans?

keyTerms.meaning: the court deals with / takes action on
the property of
interest on a loan
a loan document
a woman's marriage contract payment
food and support

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav Asi:
The court does not deal with the property of orphans,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רִבִּית אוֹכֶלֶת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: unless interest is eating away at it.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
either for a document that has interest in it,
or for a woman's כתובה, because of her food!
phrases.notes: Until the widow gets her כתובה, the estate must feed her. Paying her sooner saves the orphans money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's opinion in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that ox damage is paid from the orphans' best property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן limits collecting from orphans to two cases where waiting would cost them money. Ox damage is not one of them, so he contradicts himself.

steps.title: Switch the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the opinions. רבי יוחנן says the payment comes from the guardian's property, and רבי יוסי בר חנינא says it comes from the orphans' property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it. רבי יוחנן says: from the guardians' best property. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says: from the orphans' best property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by switching which אמורא said which opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, רבי יוחנן says the guardian pays, so the orphans' property is not collected from. That fits his rule from step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: reverse it (switch the opinions)

steps.whatToRemember: The swap is only a suggested answer. רבא rejects it in step 15, and in step 16 the original order stays: רבי יוחנן says the payment comes from the orphans' best property, because a מזיק is different from a normal debt.

phrases.english: Reverse it:
Rabbi Yochanan says: from the best property of the guardians,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מֵעֲלִיַּית יְתוֹמִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina says: from the best property of the orphans.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said the payment comes from the orphans' property, which clashes with his own rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן said the payment comes from the guardian's property, so he does not contradict himself.

steps.title: רבא rejects swapping the opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the swap from step 14 cannot be right. It makes רבי יוסי בר חנינא hold an opinion that goes against the known law, and he was an expert judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Just because רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself, you would make רבי יוסי בר חנינא into someone who made a mistake? But רבי יוסי בר חנינא was a judge who understood the law to its depths!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is pushing back against the answer in step 14, which swapped the two opinions. He says that answer causes a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, רבי יוסי בר חנינא would be saying that payment comes from the orphans' property. That goes against the known rule that we collect from orphans only for a loan with interest or a כתובה. רבא will not accept a solution that fixes רבי יוחנן by making an expert judge look wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: You make him out to be mistaken
A judge
He goes down to the depth of the law; he understands it very carefully
A contradiction of one statement against another

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן –
phrases.english: Because there is a contradiction between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: This is the contradiction from step 13: his opinion here against his rule about collecting from orphans.

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁוֵּית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא טוֹעֶה?
phrases.english: you make Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina into someone who is mistaken?
phrases.notes: After the swap he says 'from the orphans' property', which goes against the known rule about orphans.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא דַּיָּינָא הוּא,
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina is a judge,
and he goes down to the depth of the law!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּקַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מְשַׁוֵּית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא טוֹעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 14, which swapped the opinions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The swap of opinions as a way to solve the contradiction in רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The swap makes רבי יוסי בר חנינא, an expert judge, hold a view that goes against the established rule about collecting from orphans.

steps.title: Keep the original version: a damager is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the original order of opinions. He says damage done by an animal is different from a normal debt, so רבי יוחנן can still say payment comes from the orphans' best property. He then starts to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really, do not swap the opinions. A damager is different. רבי יוחנן says payment comes from the orphans' best property, because if you say it comes from the guardian's best property...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the contradiction in רבי יוחנן without swapping anyone's opinion. He begins explaining רבי יוחנן's reason, and the sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that we collect from orphans only for interest-loans or a כתובה is about normal debts. Damage caused by the orphans' ox (מזיק) is a separate category, so that rule does not apply to it. That is why רבי יוחנן's two statements no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, do not reverse the opinions
A damager is different
Best-quality property
Guardian appointed to manage the orphans' affairs

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the rule about orphans is wrong. It still applies to normal debts. Damage is simply treated as a different kind of case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings back the original version from step 12. The whole question becomes: why is damage different from a normal debt when orphans are involved?

phrases.english: Rather, actually, do not reverse,
and a damager is different.
Rabbi Yochanan said: from the orphans' best property,
because if you say from the guardian's best property,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ, וּמַזִּיק שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the swap in step 15, רבא offers a different answer to the contradiction from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction of category: damage (מזיק) is different from an ordinary debt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן's rule against collecting from orphans covers every kind of payment, so we had to swap the opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers ordinary debts. Damage is different, so רבי יוחנן can say payment comes from the orphans' best property, and the original order of opinions stays.
